title: Contact customers about unusual activity within 72 hours
description: Where monitoring identifies unusual activity requiring clarification, the customer must be contacted within 72 hours as part of the monitoring action set.
businessRule: Customer contact for unusual activity must occur within 72 hours.
trigger: Unusual activity identified through monitoring that requires customer clarification
happyPath: The analyst reviews the flagged activity and, where customer clarification is needed, contacts the customer within 72 hours, records the contact and the customer's explanation against the case.
alternateFlows: Contact would tip off the customer in a SAR context — contact suppressed under confidentiality rules
bdDAC:
Given unusual activity requiring clarification, When the analyst determines contact is needed, Then the customer is contacted within 72 hours and the contact is logged
Given a SAR has been filed on the activity, When contact is considered, Then no disclosure of the SAR is made to the customer
checklistAC:
Customer contact within 72 hours of identifying unusual activity
Contact and customer response recorded on the case
SAR confidentiality respected in any contact
validationGates:
Which activity types require customer contact versus silent investigation?
Which channel is used for customer contact and who is authorised to make it?
validation: 72-hour contact deadline tracked per case; contact prohibited where it would disclose a SAR
evidence: ["Customer contact for unusual activity (within 72 hours)","Manual review of flagged transactions"]

title: Maintain records of AI model versions, training data and performance
description: Where AI or ML is used, the platform must retain an auditable record of model versions, training data and performance metrics for regulatory inspection, held for five years.
businessRule: Model version, training data and performance metrics must be maintained for 5 years.
trigger: Model deployment, retraining or regulatory inspection
happyPath: Each model version deployed is recorded together with its training data reference and performance metrics. The record is retained for five years and can be produced on regulatory inspection.
alternateFlows: Model retrained — new version recorded alongside prior versions
bdDAC:
Given a model version is deployed, When it is registered, Then its version, training data reference and performance metrics are recorded
Given a regulatory inspection, When model records are requested, Then versions, training data and metrics from the last five years can be produced
checklistAC:
Model version registry maintained
Training data reference stored per version
Performance metrics stored per version
Records retained for 5 years
validationGates:
Confirm whether AI/ML is actually used in the MVP or only rules-based scoring
Where is training data stored and how is it version-controlled?
validation: Every deployed model version must have an associated training data reference and metrics record
evidence: ["Documentation: Model version, training data, performance metrics must be maintained for 5 years","Maintain audit trail of all AI model versions, training data, and performance metrics for regulatory inspection"]

title: Freeze accounts immediately on confirmed sanctions exposure
description: Where a customer, or a supplier they trade with, is confirmed as sanctioned during ongoing monitoring, the account must be frozen immediately and a SAR filed, with asset freeze procedures followed and no customer notification without authority approval.
businessRule: If a customer is sanctioned during monitoring the account must be frozen immediately and a SAR filed; no customer notification may be issued without authority approval.
trigger: Confirmed sanctions match during ongoing monitoring or supplier screening
happyPath: On confirmation of a sanctions match the system immediately freezes the account, blocks further transactions, creates a SAR, and initiates asset freeze procedures with escalation to the FIU. No notification is sent to the customer until an authority approves it.
alternateFlows:
Customer imports from Iran — account immediately frozen and SAR filed
Match not confirmed on review — flag cleared with rationale recorded
bdDAC:
Given a confirmed sanctions match on an active customer, When it is confirmed, Then the account is immediately frozen and a SAR is filed
Given an account has been frozen for sanctions, When customer communications are considered, Then no notification is issued without authority approval
checklistAC:
Immediate account freeze on confirmed sanctions match
SAR filing triggered automatically
Asset freeze procedures initiated and recorded
FIU escalation performed
No customer notification without authority approval
validationGates:
Who is the "authority" whose approval is needed before notifying the customer?
What are the mechanics of asset freeze in the core banking system?
validation: Freeze must take effect before any further transaction is permitted
evidence: ["If customer sanctioned during monitoring → Immediate account freeze + SAR filing","Immediate escalation if sanctions match confirmed","No customer notification without authority approval","Suppliers must be screened: If customer imports from Iran, account must be immediately frozen + SAR filed"]

title: Support configurable auto-approval rules for low-risk customers
description: The business wants to consider allowing compliance officers to configure auto-approval rules for clearly low-risk customers, such as domestic SMEs below a trade volume threshold, to hit the target of 80% of standard cases auto-approved. This is an open business decision.
trigger: Low-risk application matching configured auto-approval criteria
happyPath: A compliance officer configures auto-approval criteria for low-risk segments. Applications meeting all criteria are approved automatically without manual escalation, and the auto-approval is logged with the rule version applied.
alternateFlows: Application partially meets criteria — routed to manual review
bdDAC:
Given auto-approval rules are configured, When a low-risk application meets all criteria, Then it is approved without manual escalation and the applied rule is logged
Given an application fails any auto-approval criterion, When it is evaluated, Then it is routed to manual review
checklistAC:
Auto-approval criteria configurable by compliance officers
Auto-approvals logged with the rule version applied
80% of standard cases auto-approved measurable
Auto-approval respects the human review mandate for high-risk decisions
validationGates:
Business decision outstanding: should compliance officers be allowed to set auto-approval rules at all?
If permitted, what are the exact eligibility criteria (e.g. domestic SME, annual trade below a threshold)?
How does auto-approval reconcile with the EU AI Act human review mandate?

title: Manage correspondent banking due diligence and certification
description: For correspondent banking relationships ETFB must run a due diligence questionnaire covering the correspondent's KYC, AML training and screening processes, obtain annual certification of AML/CFT compliance, monitor all correspondent transactions, and retain the right to audit and to request transaction detail.
businessRule: Correspondent relationships require documented due diligence, annual AML/CFT certification, and must be declined where the correspondent extends into sanctioned jurisdictions.
actor: Head of Correspondent Banking / Compliance officer
trigger: A correspondent banking relationship is proposed or reaches annual review
happyPath: The correspondent completes a due diligence questionnaire on its KYC procedures, AML training and screening processes. ETFB documents the acceptable correspondent customer business types, obtains annual certification that the correspondent's AML/CFT procedures comply with standards, monitors all correspondent transactions for suspicious patterns, and can request transaction details or audit the correspondent's procedures when needed.
alternateFlows:
Correspondent relationship extends into sanctioned jurisdictions — relationship declined
Suspicious correspondent transaction — ETFB requests details from the correspondent
bdDAC:
Given a proposed correspondent relationship, When due diligence is performed, Then a completed questionnaire covering KYC procedures, AML training and screening processes is held on file
Given an existing correspondent relationship, When the annual cycle falls due, Then a certification attesting AML/CFT compliance is obtained and recorded
Given a suspicious correspondent transaction, When investigation begins, Then ETFB can formally request transaction details from the correspondent
checklistAC:
Due diligence questionnaire captured per correspondent
Acceptable correspondent customer business types documented
Annual AML/CFT certification obtained and tracked
All correspondent transactions monitored for suspicious patterns
Right to audit and right to investigate documented in the relationship record
validationGates:
What is the escalation path for approving correspondent banking relationships, and is legal involvement required?
How is the annual certification cycle tracked and enforced within the platform?
validation: Questionnaire and current annual certification must both be present for an active correspondent relationship
evidence: ["Due diligence questionnaire for correspondent: KYC procedures, AML training, screening processes","Annual certification: Correspondent attests AML/CFT procedures comply with standards","Transaction monitoring: ETFB monitors all correspondent transactions for suspicious patterns","Right to investigate: If suspicious transaction, ETFB must be able to request details from correspondent"]

title: Inform customers when AI was used in their assessment

happyPath: Where AI contributed to the assessment, the customer communication includes a statement that AI was used in their assessment decision.

AI usage flag recorded per assessment
Customer communication includes AI disclosure where applicable

What wording satisfies the disclosure obligation, and at what point in the journey is it delivered?

title: Notify rejected applicants generically and support appeals
description: Rejected customers must receive an automated notification that does not disclose the compliance reason, particularly not a sanctions basis, within the timeframe specified by law, and an appeal process must be available.
businessRule: Rejection notifications must be generic and must not disclose a sanctions reason.
trigger: Application decision is Rejected
happyPath: On rejection the system sends an automated email stating generically that the account application was not approved, within the legally specified timeframe, without disclosing the sanctions or compliance reason. The customer may use the documented appeal process.
alternateFlows: Sanctions-based rejection — reason withheld entirely and no notification without authority approval
bdDAC:
Given an application is rejected for a sanctions match, When the customer is notified, Then the notification is generic and does not disclose the sanctions reason
Given an application is rejected, When the notification is sent, Then it is issued within the timeframe specified by law
Given a rejected customer, When they wish to contest the decision, Then an appeal process is available
checklistAC:
Automated generic rejection email issued
Sanctions reasoning never disclosed to the customer
Notification issued within the legally specified timeframe
Appeal process documented and available
validationGates:
What is the legally specified notification timeframe in each target jurisdiction?
What are the steps, owner and SLA of the appeal process?
validation: Notification template restricted to generic wording; no compliance detail permitted
evidence: ["Rejected customers: Automated email with generic \"Account application not approved\" (do not disclose sanctions reason)","Customer notification of rejection decision (within timeframe specified by law)","Appeal process availability"]

title: Manage compliance escalation queue with review turnaround
description: Escalated cases — verification failures, high-risk profiles, suspicious activity, complex ownership or customers who cannot be verified — must be queued for Compliance Officer review with a defined turnaround and documented decision.
businessRule: Escalated cases must be reviewed by a Compliance Officer within 2 business days with a documented decision.
trigger: An escalation trigger occurs on a customer case
happyPath: An escalation trigger creates a case in the compliance queue. A Compliance Officer reviews it within 2 business days and records a documented decision to approve, reject or request additional information. Case assignment and decision are logged.
alternateFlows:
Case requires senior compliance review — escalated further
Customer rejected — notification and appeal process apply
bdDAC:
Given a verification failure, high-risk profile, suspicious transaction, complex beneficial ownership or unverifiable customer, When the trigger fires, Then an escalation case is created in the compliance queue
Given an escalated case, When it is reviewed, Then the Compliance Officer decision is recorded within 2 business days with documentation
checklistAC:
All defined escalation triggers create queue cases
Escalation case assignment within the 2 business day SLA
Decision documented as approve, reject or request additional information
Case audit trail complete
validationGates:
How are escalation cases assigned across 8-10 analysts and 1-2 officers at 50-100 reviews per day?
What is the escalation path when the 2 business day review SLA is missed?
validation: Every escalation must record a decision type and rationale before closure
evidence: ["Escalated cases reviewed by Compliance Officer within 2 business days","Documentation of decision (approve/reject/request additional info)","Escalation case assignment within SLA (2 business days)"]

title: Provide a transaction monitoring dashboard for analysts
description: Analysts need a single dashboard showing flagged transactions sorted by risk, customer transaction history over standard periods, baseline versus current pattern comparison and their own action tracking, so review is efficient at 20-50 flags per day.
trigger: Analyst begins their review queue
happyPath: The analyst opens the monitoring dashboard and sees flagged transactions auto-sorted by risk score, each with its flag reason. They can drill into the customer's 30, 90 or 365 day transaction history, compare baseline against current pattern, add notes, and mark the item reviewed, approved or escalated to SAR.

Given flagged transactions exist, When the analyst opens the dashboard, Then all flagged transactions are shown with their risk reason, auto-sorted by risk score
Given a flagged transaction, When the analyst reviews it, Then they can add a manual note and record the action taken (reviewed, approved, escalated to SAR)
Given a customer under review, When the analyst opens their history, Then 30, 90 and 365 day views are available with baseline versus current pattern comparison
checklistAC:
Flagged transactions auto-sorted by risk score
Flag reason shown for each item
30/90/365 day transaction history available
Baseline versus current pattern comparison displayed
Analyst notes and action tracking recorded
validationGates:
Is behavioural pattern comparison in MVP scope, given advanced monitoring and behavioural analytics are listed for Phase 2?
Page-level performance target for the dashboard under 2000-5000 transactions/day

description: Advanced verification capabilities are explicitly excluded from the MVP: machine-learning tamper detection, biometric face matching and video identity verification are deferred to later phases. Given the MVP release, When verification capability is assessed, Then advanced ML-based tamper detection, biometric face matching and video identity verification are not present
Given remote onboarding in the MVP, When identity is verified, Then verification relies on document OCR, data matching and third-party checks only

Advanced tamper detection excluded from MVP
Biometric face matching excluded from MVP
Video identity verification excluded from MVP
Only basic pixel-level tamper consistency checking implemented in MVP
validationGates:

title: Integrate with core banking, payment rails, document management and reporting systems
description: The KYC platform must integrate with ETFB's surrounding systems: account creation into the customer management system, transaction monitoring with the payment rails, document storage with retrieval for regulators, and SAR filing with the financial intelligence reporting system.

happyPath: Account creation writes through to the core banking customer management system; the monitoring engine consumes transaction events from the payment rails; documents are held in a document management system able to produce records within 10 days; SAR filings are routed through the financial intelligence reporting integration; and external screening, PEP and national ID registry services are called as needed.
alternateFlows: An integration is unavailable — fallback and manual handling apply per feature
bdDAC:
Given an account is approved, When activation completes, Then the customer record is created in the core banking customer management system
Given a transaction posts on the payment rails, When the event is received, Then the monitoring engine evaluates it
Given a SAR is submitted, When filing occurs, Then it is transmitted through the financial intelligence reporting integration and the confirmation is stored
checklistAC:
Core banking / customer management integration implemented
Payment rails transaction feed integrated
Document management integration supporting 10-day retrieval
SAR filing integration with financial intelligence reporting
External screening, PEP and national ID registry integrations in place

Which specific core banking and payment systems are in scope and what are their interface contracts?

title: Automatically verify customer-supplied data against document extraction
description: An automated verification engine must compare customer-declared data against OCR-extracted document data and flag inconsistencies, so compliance staff only manually review exceptions. It also checks ID validity and document recency.
businessRule: An ID expired by more than 6 months is rejected; proof of address must be dated within the last 3 months.
trigger: Identity and address documents have been uploaded and OCR extraction has completed
happyPath: The engine matches name (exact plus phonetic, allowing one character variance), date of birth (exact match only) and address (street number plus postal code), compares ID expiry against the current date, and checks that proof of address is less than three months old. If all checks pass, the customer advances to screening; each check is written to the audit log with timestamp, check type, result and confidence score.
alternateFlows:
Name mismatch, expired ID or inconsistent information flags the case for manual review
ID expired more than 6 months is rejected
Proof of address older than 3 months triggers re-submission
bdDAC:
Given customer-supplied data and OCR output, When verification runs, Then it completes within 30 seconds per customer
Given a customer whose declared date of birth does not exactly match the document, When verification runs, Then the case is flagged for manual review
Given an ID document expired more than 6 months ago, When verification runs, Then the document is rejected
Given verification has not passed, When the customer attempts to progress, Then the account remains in "pending verification" and cannot advance
checklistAC:
Name matched exact plus phonetic with 1 character variance allowed
Date of birth matched exact only
Address matched on street number and postal code
ID rejected if expired more than 6 months
Proof of address must be less than 3 months old
False positive rate below 5% of valid customers
Every check logged with timestamp, check type, result and confidence score
validationGates:
Is one character variance acceptable to compliance for name matching, or is a stricter rule required?
What happens to IDs expired by less than 6 months — accept, flag, or reject?
validation: Name: exact + phonetic, 1 character variance; DOB: exact match only; Address: street number + postal code; ID expiry vs current date; proof of address < 3 months old
evidence: ["Compare ID expiry against current date (reject if expired >6 months)","Document recency check: Proof of address <3 months old","Verification completes in <30 seconds per customer","Unverified customers cannot proceed to next step (account remains \"pending verification\")"]

title: Manage the account onboarding status lifecycle
description: Each application must move through a defined set of statuses from Pending CIV through to Active, Rejected or On Hold, with automated transitions where the system can determine the outcome and manual transitions where an officer decision is required. happyPath: An application starts at Pending CIV, moves automatically to Pending Screening when the ID is verified and to Pending CDD Review when screening completes, then to Pending Document Collection and Pending Compliance Approval. Application Rejected — customer notified

Given any status change, When it is recorded, Then timestamp, new status, previous status, changed by and reason are stored

All eight defined statuses implemented
Automated transitions for CIV → Screening → CDD Review
Manual transition only from Pending Compliance Approval to Active or Rejected
Account status visible in the compliance dashboard
Full status change audit trail
validationGates:
What triggers a move to On Hold, and who has authority to set and clear it?
Can an application move backwards in the lifecycle, and under what conditions?
validation: Only defined statuses permitted; every transition must record actor and timestamp
evidence: ["\"Pending CIV\" - Awaiting ID/address verification","Account status visible in dashboard for compliance team","Status change audit trail: Timestamp, status, previous status, changed by, reason (if applicable)"]

title: Screen suppliers and transaction counterparties
description: Beyond the customer, ETFB must screen suppliers and transaction counterparties against sanctions lists, because trade finance exposure arises through the customer's supply chain. Coverage must reach 100% of customers, suppliers and counterparties.
businessRule: Sanctions screening must cover all suppliers and transaction counterparties, not only the customer; new suppliers in high-risk countries require pre-approval.

alternateFlows:
Customer imports from Iran — account immediately frozen and SAR filed
Supplier identified as an SOE — flagged as government-connected requiring enhanced review

Given a transaction counterparty, When screening is invoked, Then a result is returned within 5 seconds per counterparty
Given a supplier appears on a sanctions list, When the match is confirmed, Then the customer's account is frozen and a SAR is filed
Given a new supplier in a high-risk country, When it is added, Then pre-approval is required before transacting
checklistAC:
Customers, suppliers and transaction counterparties all screened
National lists for Germany, France and Italy included
Russia sectoral sanctions covered
Real-time counterparty screening under 5 seconds
Weekly re-screening of suppliers
SOE suppliers flagged for enhanced review
New high-risk-country suppliers require pre-approval

Should customers be required to provide a supplier list, or is it optional?

How are SOEs identified — from which data source?

title: Support restricted account opening and freeze during review
description: The platform must support an exception path allowing a limited-use, restricted account to be opened pending verification, with authority to freeze the account during review, reverse the opening after review, and communicate restriction reasons to the customer.

title: Apply Enhanced Due Diligence for high-risk relationships

trigger: Customer needs to provide identity or address documentation during onboarding
happyPath: The user uploads a PDF, JPG, PNG or TIFF document up to 20MB. The system detects the document type (passport, national ID, driver's license), runs quality checks for resolution, readability and visible corners, performs basic pixel-level tamper detection, and extracts name, date of birth, expiry date, ID number and issue country by OCR. Documents are stored in an encrypted bucket separate from profile data and an audit entry is written.
alternateFlows:
Document fails quality checks — a clear error message is shown (e.g. "Blurry document - retake required") and the customer must retake it
OCR fails — the case is routed to the compliance analyst manual review queue
bdDAC:
Given a standard 5MB document in a supported format, When the user uploads it, Then upload completes in under 10 seconds and the document type is detected automatically
Given a Western European ID document, When OCR runs, Then extraction accuracy of name, DOB, expiry date, ID number and issue country exceeds 95%
Given OCR fails on an uploaded document, When processing completes, Then the case is placed in the compliance analyst manual review queue
Given an uploaded document is blurry, When quality checks run, Then the document is rejected with a clear error message
checklistAC:
PDF, JPG, PNG and TIFF accepted up to 20MB per document
Minimum 300 DPI, all text readable, four corners visible enforced
OCR extracts name, DOB, expiry date, ID number and issue country
Audit trail captures upload time, document type, OCR confidence score and analyst review timestamp
Documents stored in encrypted storage separate from customer profile data with 5-year retention
validationGates:
Which document languages must OCR support beyond English/German?
What OCR confidence threshold routes a document to manual review?
validation: Max 20MB per document; formats PDF/JPG/PNG/TIFF; minimum 300 DPI; all text readable; four corners visible; basic pixel-level tamper consistency check
evidence: ["Supported formats: PDF, JPG, PNG, TIFF (max 20MB per document)","OCR extraction of key fields: Name, DOB, Expiry date, ID number, Issue country","Document upload completes in <10 seconds for standard 5MB file","Failed OCR triggers manual review workflow (compliance analyst review queue)"]

title: Schedule and enforce periodic customer risk reviews
description: The platform must schedule recurring customer reviews at a frequency driven by risk level, notify the assigned analyst in advance, present a review checklist and prevent the review from being dismissed without completion or escalation.
businessRule: Review frequency is determined by CDD level: Standard quarterly, Medium bi-weekly, Enhanced monthly.
trigger: Scheduled review due date approaching for a customer
happyPath: The system schedules the next review based on the customer's CDD level, emails the assigned analyst five days before the due date, and presents a review checklist covering transaction activity summary, any flags, risk profile changes and continued relationship justification. The analyst records an action — accept with no changes, update risk score, escalate to senior review, or close the account — with comments and approval.
alternateFlows:
Analyst escalates to senior review
Review identifies material change — risk score updated and CDD level re-assigned
Review results in account closure
bdDAC:
Given a customer review due in five days, When the scheduler runs, Then an email notification is sent to the assigned analyst
Given a due review, When the analyst attempts to dismiss it, Then the system prevents dismissal and requires completion or escalation
Given a review is completed, When it is saved, Then the completion date, findings, action taken and approver are recorded
checklistAC:
Review frequency derived from CDD level
Notification sent 5 days before due date
Review checklist includes transaction activity, flags, profile changes and relationship justification
Reviews cannot be dismissed — completion or escalation required
Audit trail records review completion date, findings, action and approver
validationGates:
Resolve conflicting review frequencies for Medium CDD: bi-weekly (PRD 6.2 and Persona 2) versus quarterly (PRD 3.1 risk bands) versus monthly (regulatory brief for EDD)
Confirm weekly review requirement for multinational customers with transactions over €1M
validation: Every active customer must have a scheduled next review date; reviews cannot be closed without an action and comments
evidence: ["Review notifications sent 5 days before due date","Compliance analyst cannot dismiss review (must complete or escalate)","Standard CDD: Quarterly review","Medium CDD: Bi-weekly reviews"]

title: Produce Currency Transaction Reports for threshold breaches
description: Transactions at or above the €10,000 threshold must be documented and monitored for CTR purposes, with cumulative reporting where the jurisdiction requires it, and may escalate to a SAR if a pattern is detected. Built-in CTR templates and submission tracking are required.
businessRule: All transactions above €10,000 (cumulative daily) must be reported under EU requirements.
trigger: Transaction reaches or exceeds the €10,000 reporting threshold
happyPath: The system identifies transactions of €10,000 or equivalent in a single transaction, documents them for CTR purposes and monitors them cumulatively. Where a pattern indicating money laundering emerges, the case is escalated to SAR. Reports are generated from built-in templates and tracked to submission.
alternateFlows: Cumulative daily activity crosses the threshold across multiple transactions — cumulative reporting applies
bdDAC:
Given a single transaction of €10,000 or more, When it posts, Then it is documented and monitored for CTR reporting
Given cumulative daily transactions exceed €10,000, When the threshold is crossed, Then cumulative reporting is applied where the jurisdiction requires it
Given a CTR pattern indicates possible laundering, When reviewed, Then the case can be escalated to SAR
checklistAC:
€10,000 single transaction threshold detected and documented
Cumulative daily tracking supported
CTR templates built in with submission tracking
Escalation route from CTR to SAR available
validationGates:
Which of ETFB's jurisdictions require cumulative CTR reporting versus single-transaction only?
Confirm whether CTR filing is automated or analyst-initiated
validation: Threshold €10,000 or equivalent per single transaction; cumulative daily tracking where required
evidence: ["Threshold: €10,000 or equivalent in single transaction","Requirement: Document and monitor; may trigger SAR if pattern detected","Regulatory reporting: Built-in SAR/CTR templates + FIU submission tracking"]

title: File Suspicious Activity Reports with FIU submission tracking
description: When an officer marks activity as suspicious the platform must create a SAR from a template pre-populated with the transaction details, support submission to the Financial Intelligence Unit within the regulatory timeframe, and log the filing confirmation. SAR filing is confidential and must never be disclosed to the customer.
businessRule: SAR filing is confidential and must not be disclosed to the customer; SARs must be filed within the regulatory timeframe, typically 5 working days in the EU.
trigger: Officer marks a transaction or pattern as suspicious
happyPath: The officer marks the transaction as "Suspicious", which creates a SAR with customer information, transaction details, reason for suspicion, amount and dates auto-populated from the case. The officer completes and submits it to the FIU within the required timeframe (typically 5 working days in the EU), and the filing confirmation with FIU reference number is logged.
alternateFlows:
Confirmed sanctions match — immediate escalation, FIU reporting and asset freeze, with no customer notification without authority approval
Structuring confirmed — SAR filed within 5 working days
bdDAC:
Given a transaction marked as "Suspicious", When the officer confirms, Then a SAR is created with transaction details auto-populated
Given a SAR is submitted, When submission completes, Then the timestamp, FIU reference number and SAR contents are stored and auditable
Given a SAR has been filed, When customer-facing communications are generated, Then no reference to the SAR is disclosed to the customer
checklistAC:
SAR created from officer suspicious marking
Template auto-populated with customer info, transaction details, reason for suspicion, amount and dates
SAR submitted within the regulatory timeframe with submission tracking
Filing confirmation and FIU reference number logged
SAR confidentiality enforced — no customer disclosure
100% of SARs filed within regulatory timeline is measurable
validationGates:
What is the approved process for SAR filing? (to be confirmed with the compliance legal team)
Is FIU submission electronic and integrated, or manual with tracking only?
Which national FIU formats must be supported across ETFB's markets?
validation: SAR mandatory fields: customer info, transaction details, reason for suspicion, amount, dates; filing confirmation must be recorded
evidence: ["Officer marks transaction as \"Suspicious\" → Creates SAR","SAR template auto-populated with transaction details","Confidentiality: SAR filing is confidential; disclosure to customer prohibited","SAR filing auditable (timestamp, FIU reference number, contents)"]

title: Assign CDD level automatically from risk score
description: The system must assign a CDD level (Simplified, Standard, Medium or Enhanced) from the risk score, driving the documentation checklist, monitoring frequency, escalation authority and approval timeline. The assignment is a recommendation the officer can change with a documented reason.
businessRule: CDD level is assigned from the risk score band and determines documentation, monitoring frequency, escalation authority and approval timeline; officers may override with a documented reason.
trigger: Risk score calculated for a customer
happyPath: The system maps the risk score to a CDD level and stores it on the customer profile with the reason. The CDD level then determines the required documentation checklist, the monitoring frequency, the escalation authority and the approval timeline. The customer cannot progress until a level is assigned.
alternateFlows:
Compliance officer changes the assigned level with a documented reason, which is logged
Customer qualifies for Simplified CDD under an exemption category
bdDAC:
Given a risk score of 30, When CDD assignment runs, Then Medium CDD is assigned with enhanced quarterly monitoring
Given a customer without an assigned CDD level, When they attempt to proceed, Then the system blocks progression
Given a compliance officer changes the CDD level, When they save, Then the change, reason, timestamp and user are logged
checklistAC:
CDD level assigned before the customer can proceed to the next step
Every customer has a level — no "unknown" status exists
Officer changes to level are logged with reason
CDD level and reason displayed on the customer profile
Approval timeline set by level (standard 24 hours; enhanced 48-72 hours)
validationGates:
Reconcile the four-level model (Simplified/Standard/Medium/Enhanced) with the three-band score mapping (0-25, 26-60, 61-100) — where does Simplified CDD fit?
Which exemption criteria qualify a customer for Simplified CDD in ETFB's markets?
validation: No customer may hold an "unknown" CDD level; level must be set before progression
evidence: ["System automatically assigns CDD level based on risk score","CDD level assigned before customer can proceed to next step","All customers assigned a level (no \"unknown\" status)","Approval timeline (standard review: 24 hours; enhanced: 48-72 hours)"]

title: Collect mandatory customer identification data
description: The platform must capture the full set of customer identification attributes required for Customer Identification and Verification (CIV) before an account can be opened, including identity, residence, tax and economic-purpose data. This data forms the basis for verification, risk scoring and ongoing monitoring.
businessRule: Permanent home address must be a physical address; P.O. Boxes are not acceptable.
trigger: Customer requests an account online or via a bank representative
happyPath: The customer (or onboarding agent) submits full legal name, permanent home address, date of birth, place of birth where required, nationality/tax residency, occupation and economic purpose of the account, a source of funds declaration and PEP status. The captured profile is stored against the customer record and passed to verification and risk scoring.
alternateFlows:
Customer supplies a P.O. Box instead of a permanent home address — address is not acceptable
Customer unable to verify (missing documentation, no legitimate address) is escalated
bdDAC:
Given a new customer application, When the onboarding agent submits the identification form, Then full legal name, permanent home address, date of birth, nationality/tax residency, occupation and economic purpose, source of funds declaration and PEP status are all captured and stored
Given a customer supplies a P.O. Box as their permanent home address, When the form is submitted, Then the address is rejected as invalid
checklistAC:
All mandatory CIV fields are captured for every application
P.O. Box addresses are not accepted as permanent home address
Place of birth is captured where the jurisdiction requires it
Source of funds declaration and PEP status are recorded on the profile
validationGates:
Which jurisdictions require place of birth?
What are the permitted values / formats for nationality and tax residency?
Is PEP status self-declared by the customer, derived from screening, or both?
validation: Mandatory fields: full legal name, permanent home address (not P.O. Box), date of birth, nationality/tax residency, occupation and economic purpose, source of funds declaration, PEP status
evidence: ["Full legal name (surname and given name(s))","Permanent home address (not P.O. Box)","Occupation and economic purpose of account"]

title: Train compliance staff on the platform and AML obligations
description: All compliance staff must understand their AML/CFT obligations and be trained on the new KYC platform before go-live, with training refreshed as regulations change. Go-live depends on the team being trained and comfortable with the platform.
businessRule: All decisions must be defensible in a regulatory audit, which requires trained staff.
trigger: Platform go-live preparation, or a regulatory change
happyPath: Training is delivered in the go-live preparation week covering AML/CFT obligations and platform operation for both recent hires and experienced staff. Five analysts participate in user acceptance testing. Training is refreshed whenever regulations change.
alternateFlows: Regulation changes post go-live — training content refreshed and redelivered
bdDAC:
Given the go-live date, When readiness is assessed, Then all compliance team members are trained and comfortable with the platform
Given a regulatory change, When it takes effect, Then training material is refreshed for affected staff
checklistAC:
All staff trained on AML/CFT obligations
All staff trained on the new KYC platform
Five analysts complete user acceptance testing
At least 50 customer files successfully onboarded in UAT
Training refreshed on regulatory change
validationGates:
Who delivers and owns the training curriculum?
How is training completion evidenced for regulatory purposes?
validation: Go-live gated on completed training and successful UAT
evidence: ["Training requirement:** All staff must understand AML/CFT obligations","At least 50 customer files successfully onboarded in UAT"]

title: Support document languages required for target markets
description: Document processing must handle the languages of the customers ETFB serves. The MVP working assumption is English and German only, which is a live open question given operations across 12 EU countries plus UK, Switzerland and Turkey.
trigger: A document is submitted in a language other than the supported set
happyPath: Documents in supported languages are processed by OCR and verification normally.
alternateFlows: Document in an unsupported language — routed to manual review
bdDAC:
Given a document in a supported language, When OCR runs, Then extraction meets the accuracy target
Given a document in an unsupported language, When it is submitted, Then it is routed to manual review rather than silently failing
checklistAC:
Supported document languages documented
Unsupported languages routed to manual handling
validationGates:
Do we need to support multiple languages for documents beyond English and German?
Which languages are mandatory given operations across 12 EU countries plus UK, Switzerland and Turkey?
validation: Language support set must be explicitly configured; out-of-scope languages must not be auto-processed
evidence: ["Do we need to support multiple languages for documents? (Assume English/German initially for MVP)","OCR accuracy >95% for Western European ID formats"]

title: Reduce onboarding and manual review time to target cycle times
description: The commercial purpose of the platform is to cut onboarding time drastically: from a 5-7 day manual process to under 24 hours overall, with standard customers approved within 4 hours and manual document review reduced to under 10 minutes per customer, while cutting false rejections.
trigger: Business case measurement of onboarding performance
happyPath: Automation of verification, screening and risk assessment reduces manual review time so that standard customers are approved in under 4 hours, medium and high risk customers within 24 hours, manual document review takes under 10 minutes per customer, and false rejections fall to under 3%, allowing the existing team to support 500 new customers per month without hiring.
alternateFlows: High-risk and correspondent cases retain longer approval timelines (2-7 days)
bdDAC:
Given a standard customer application, When onboarding completes, Then the elapsed time from application start to account active is under 4 hours
Given a measurement month, When manual review effort is measured, Then average manual document review time is under 10 minutes per customer
Given a measurement month, When rejections are analysed, Then the false rejection rate is below 3%
checklistAC:
Standard customer approval under 4 hours measured from application start
Medium/high customer approval under 24 hours
Manual document review under 10 minutes per customer
False rejection rate below 3%
80% of standard cases auto-approved without manual escalation
Existing compliance team supports 500 new customers per month
validationGates:
Reconcile the multiple cycle time targets across documents (<2 hours in the PRD vision, <4 hours and <24 hours in the ETFB business case)
How is 'application start' defined for measurement purposes?
validation: Cycle time and rejection metrics measured and reported against targets
evidence: ["Current manual process takes 5-7 days; target is <24 hours.","Standard customer approval <4 hours (50% reduction from current 8 hours)","Manual document review time <10 minutes per customer (currently 25 minutes)","reduce manual review time from 48 hours to <2 hours for standard customers"]

title: Provide customers a self-service application status view
description: Customers must be able to see the progress of their application in a self-service portal, showing generic status only and never internal compliance detail such as screening results or risk scores.
businessRule: Customers see generic application status only; compliance details are not disclosed.
trigger: Customer logs into the onboarding portal
happyPath: The customer opens the portal and sees a generic progress indicator for their application together with any outstanding document requests, without exposure to compliance-internal information.
alternateFlows: Application rejected — customer sees a generic outcome without the compliance reason
bdDAC:
Given an application in progress, When the customer views the portal, Then a generic status is shown without compliance details
Given an application flagged for sanctions review, When the customer views the portal, Then no indication of screening or sanctions reasoning is displayed
checklistAC:
Self-service status view available to customers
Only generic statuses exposed externally
No compliance-internal data (risk score, screening results, PEP status) visible to the customer
validationGates: Which generic status labels are approved for customer display?
validation: Portal must not expose sanctions, PEP or risk score information
evidence: ["Customer can view application status in self-service portal (generic status, not compliance details)","Checklist displays to customer in onboarding portal"]

title: Route screening matches by confidence with human review before rejection
description: Screening results must be triaged by match confidence: exact matches reject, high-confidence fuzzy matches escalate to a compliance officer, and low-confidence matches are logged only. A human compliance decision is required before a customer is rejected on a sanctions basis.
businessRule: Exact match = immediate rejection; high-confidence fuzzy match = escalate to compliance review; low-confidence match = log and monitor only. No rejection without human compliance review.
trigger: Screening returns a potential match
happyPath: The system classifies the match by similarity score. High-confidence fuzzy matches create a compliance review task; the officer reviews the evidence and decides within 2 hours whether the match is a false positive or confirmed. The decision and rationale are logged.
alternateFlows:
Low confidence match below threshold — logged and monitored, no escalation
Confirmed sanctions match — immediate escalation, reporting to the FIU and asset freeze procedures, with no customer notification without authority approval
bdDAC:
Given a fuzzy match above the high-confidence threshold, When screening completes, Then the case is escalated to compliance review rather than auto-rejected
Given a match below the low-confidence threshold, When screening completes, Then the match is logged and monitored with no escalation
Given a false positive review is open, When the compliance officer reviews it, Then a decision is recorded within 2 hours
checklistAC:
Confidence bands configured and applied to every match
Human compliance review occurs before any sanctions-based rejection
False positive decision recorded within 2 hours
Confirmed matches trigger FIU reporting and asset freeze procedures
validationGates:
Resolve conflicting match thresholds: >85% similarity for escalation in the PRD versus >90% high-confidence match in the ETFB business document
Who has authority to approve customer notification on a confirmed sanctions match?
validation: Similarity thresholds applied per match band; compliance officer decision required within 2 hours
evidence: ["High-confidence fuzzy match (>85% similarity): Escalate to compliance review","False positive review: Human compliance review before rejection","Match threshold: Exact or high-confidence match (>90% similarity) only","False positive review: Compliance officer decision within 2 hours"]

title: Support Simplified CDD for exempt low-risk customer categories
description: Certain low-risk categories qualify for simplified due diligence with a reduced documentation set. The platform must recognise these exemption categories and generate a lighter checklist accordingly.
businessRule: Simplified CDD applies to low-risk EU/EEA customers, under-18s with parental verification, non-profits with government oversight and public companies listed on major exchanges.
trigger: Customer falls within a recognised simplified CDD exemption category
happyPath: The system identifies the customer as an exempt category — low-risk EU/EEA customer, under-18 with parental verification, non-profit with government oversight, or a public company listed on a major exchange — and applies the Simplified CDD checklist requiring ID only, without proof of address.
alternateFlows: Jurisdiction does not permit the exemption — Standard CDD applies
bdDAC:
Given a customer who is a public company listed on a major exchange, When CDD is assigned, Then Simplified CDD is applied and only ID is required
Given a customer under 18, When Simplified CDD is applied, Then parental verification is recorded
checklistAC:
Exemption categories configurable and auditable
Simplified CDD checklist requires ID only, no proof of address
Reason for exemption recorded on the customer profile
validationGates:
Which of ETFB's jurisdictions permit each simplified CDD exemption?
Clarify the note that "mutual consent not required for some jurisdictions" — what does this mean operationally?
How does Simplified CDD interact with the 0-100 risk score bands?
validation: Simplified CDD: ID only, no proof of address required
evidence: ["Low-risk customers in EU/EEA","Age <18 with parental verification","Public companies listed on major exchanges"]

title: Maintain a complete audit trail of decisions and profile changes
description: Every decision, user action and change to a customer profile must be logged with timestamp, user and rationale so that decisions are defensible in a regulatory audit. Audit coverage must be 100% of decisions and of customer creation events.
businessRule: All decisions must be logged with timestamp, user and rationale and must be defensible in a regulatory audit.
trigger: Any user action, decision or profile change
happyPath: For each event the system records the date and time, the field changed with old and new values, the analyst or officer responsible, the decision outcome and the rationale. All user actions including view, update and export are logged with timestamp and user ID and are queryable for audit sampling.
alternateFlows: Auditor requests a random sample of customer files — audit trail retrieved per case
bdDAC:
Given a customer profile field is changed, When the change is saved, Then the date, time, field changed, old value, new value and analyst are recorded
Given any compliance decision is taken, When it is recorded, Then timestamp, user and rationale are stored
Given a user views or exports customer data, When the action occurs, Then it is logged with timestamp and user ID
checklistAC:
100% of decisions logged with timestamp, user and rationale
100% of customer creation events captured with analyst and timestamp
Profile change log captures field, old value and new value
View, update and export actions logged
Audit trail completeness verifiable by random sampling
validationGates:
How long must audit logs be retained relative to the 5-year document retention period?
Is the audit trail exempt from GDPR deletion requests, as implied?
validation: No decision or profile change may be committed without an attributable user and timestamp
evidence: ["Changes to customer profile: date, time, field changed, old/new value, analyst","Audit trail: All decisions logged with timestamp, user, and rationale","Audit logging: All user actions logged (view, update, export) with timestamp + user ID","100% of customer creation events captured with analyst/timestamp audit trail"]

title: Retain documents for five years with 10-day regulator retrieval
description: KYC documentation and records must be retained for a minimum of five years after account closure, held in encrypted digital storage separate from profile data, and retrievable within 10 days of a regulator request.
businessRule: Records must be retained for a minimum of 5 years after account closure and be retrievable within 10 days for regulator requests.
trigger: Account closure, or a regulator request for records
happyPath: Documents are stored in an encrypted bucket separate from customer profile data under a five-year retention policy measured from account closure. On a regulator request, the required documents and audit records are located and produced within 10 days.
alternateFlows:
Jurisdiction requires 7-10 year retention — longer period applies
Historical data older than 2 years archived to cold storage while remaining retrievable
bdDAC:
Given an account is closed, When the retention clock starts, Then documents are retained for a minimum of five years from closure
Given a regulator requests customer records, When the request is actioned, Then the documents are retrievable within 10 days
Given data older than two years, When archival runs, Then it is moved to cold storage and remains retrievable within the 10-day SLA
checklistAC:
Five-year minimum retention post-closure enforced and verifiable
Documents stored encrypted and separate from profile data
10-day retrieval SLA for regulator requests met
Cold storage archival for data older than 2 years
Retention policy log maintained
validationGates:
Which jurisdictions in ETFB's footprint require 7-10 years rather than 5?
How is the retention clock managed for customers with no closure event?
validation: Retention minimum 5 years post-closure; retrieval SLA 10 days
evidence: ["Minimum 5 years after account closure (or transaction completion)","Digital storage acceptable; must be retrievable within 10 days for regulator requests","Storage: Encrypted S3 bucket, separate from customer profile data, 5-year retention policy","Archival: Historical data (>2 years old) archived to cold storage (cost optimization)"]

title: Enforce encryption, role-based access and PII masking
description: Customer data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, access must be controlled by role, and sensitive personal fields must be masked in the interface unless the analyst holds explicit permission.
businessRule: Sensitive fields (ID number, DOB) are masked in the UI unless the analyst has explicit permission.
trigger: Any access to or storage of customer data
happyPath: Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or above. Users are granted analyst, compliance officer or admin roles that determine what they can see and do. Sensitive fields such as ID number and date of birth are masked in the UI unless the user holds explicit permission to view them.
alternateFlows: Analyst without permission attempts to view an unmasked ID number — access denied and the attempt logged
bdDAC:
Given customer data is stored, When it is written, Then it is encrypted at rest using AES-256
Given data is transmitted, When a request is made, Then TLS 1.2 or higher is enforced
Given an analyst without explicit permission views a customer record, When the record renders, Then ID number and date of birth are masked
checklistAC:
AES-256 encryption at rest
TLS 1.2+ in transit
Role-based access control for analyst, compliance officer and admin
Sensitive fields masked in UI without explicit permission
Access attempts logged
validationGates:
Which additional fields count as sensitive and require masking?
What approval process grants an analyst unmasked-view permission?
validation: Encryption at rest AES-256; in transit TLS 1.2+; role-based permissions enforced on every access
evidence: ["Data encryption: At-rest (AES-256), in-transit (TLS 1.2+)","Access control: Role-based (analyst, compliance officer, admin)","PII handling: Sensitive fields (ID number, DOB) masked in UI unless analyst has explicit permission"]

title: Support GDPR customer data deletion on account closure
description: On account closure the platform must be able to delete customer personal data on request in line with GDPR, while preserving the audit trail required for regulatory purposes.
businessRule: Customer data deletion is available upon account closure, except for the audit trail.
trigger: Customer data deletion request following account closure
happyPath: On a valid deletion request after account closure, the system deletes the customer's personal data while retaining the audit trail and any records subject to the statutory retention period, and records the deletion action.
alternateFlows: Deletion request conflicts with the 5-year retention obligation — retention takes precedence and the exception is recorded
bdDAC:
Given an account is closed and a valid deletion request is made, When deletion is executed, Then customer personal data is deleted while the audit trail is retained
Given data is subject to statutory retention, When deletion is requested, Then the retained records are excluded from deletion and the exception is documented
checklistAC:
Deletion capability available on account closure
Audit trail excluded from deletion
Deletion actions logged
Conflicts with statutory retention documented
validationGates:
How are GDPR erasure rights reconciled with the 5-10 year AML retention obligation, field by field?
Who approves and executes deletion requests?
validation: Audit trail and statutory retention records must be preserved through deletion
evidence: ["GDPR compliance: Customer data deletion available upon account closure (except audit trail)","Data retention: 5 years post-account closure (regulatory requirement)"]

title: Notify customers of document status changes and manage re-submission
description: Customers must be told, by email, whenever a document's status changes and given the specific reason a document was rejected, so they can re-submit correctly first time. This directly addresses the assumption that roughly 30% of customers will need to re-submit.
trigger: A document status changes to Rejected, Received or all documents Verified
happyPath: When a document is rejected, the system emails the customer with the specific reason (for example that the proof of address is too old and must be dated within three months) and sets the item to Re-submission Required. The customer uploads a replacement, the analyst reviews it, and the customer is notified again when all documents are verified.
alternateFlows: Repeated rejection — analyst adds a manual note or request for clarification
bdDAC:
Given a document is rejected because the proof of address is older than three months, When the rejection is saved, Then the customer receives an email stating that specific reason
Given all documents become verified, When the final verification is recorded, Then the customer is notified by email
checklistAC:
Email notification sent for each document status change
Rejection notifications state the specific reason
Re-submitted documents re-enter the verification workflow
Notification events recorded in the audit trail
validationGates:
Which languages must customer notifications support?
Are notification channels limited to email, or also portal/SMS?
validation: Rejection reason is mandatory and included in the customer notification
evidence: ["Re-submission workflow: Rejected documents trigger customer notification with specific reasons (e.g., \"Proof of address too old - must be dated within 3 months\")","Customer receives email notification for each status change (document rejected, re-submission received, all docs verified)"]

title: Meet platform performance and concurrency targets

Given normal load, When an analyst opens the dashboard or performs a customer search, Then the page loads in under 3 seconds
Given the required number of concurrent analysts are logged in, When they work simultaneously, Then performance targets are still met
Given a transaction posts, When monitoring evaluates it, Then flagging completes within 30 seconds
checklistAC:
Page load under 3 seconds for dashboard and customer search
Screening response under 5 seconds
Transaction flagging within 30 seconds of posting
Concurrency target met and load tested
Database indexed on customer ID, transaction date and risk score
validationGates:
Resolve conflicting concurrency targets: 50 concurrent analysts (PRD) versus 15 concurrent analysts (ETFB operational metrics)
Define peak load assumptions for 200-500 new customers/month and 2000-5000 transactions/day

happyPath: The platform sustains 99.9% measured uptime, with availability monitored and reported.
alternateFlows: Planned maintenance windows — treatment against the uptime target to be defined

99.9% uptime target defined and monitored
Availability reporting available to the business
